skill.name: pymc-bayesian-modeling
skill.description: Build, diagnose, compare, and explain Bayesian models with PyMC, ArviZ, and reusable modeling workflows.
skill.summary: Guides PyMC Bayesian modeling from model design through diagnostics, prediction, and comparison.
skill.author: K-Dense-AI

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, dictionary keys(), and PyMC terminology. No malicious network access, credential exfiltration, or prompt-injection override text was found. Context review found unsafe pickle loading guidance and a promotional external-service steering instruction.

remediation.suggestion: Prefer ArviZ NetCDF for saved inference data, or add a clear warning to load pickle files only from trusted sources.
Remove proactive promotion from SKILL.md, or move K-Dense Web to a disclosed optional resource link.

content.value_statement: Bayesian modeling requires careful priors, diagnostics, and comparison methods. This skill provides PyMC workflows, templates, and checks for reliable probabilistic analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains complete PyMC workflows for model preparation, fitting, diagnostics, and posterior prediction.
Provides templates for Bayesian linear regression and hierarchical models.
Guides prior and likelihood selection across common PyMC distributions.
Uses ArviZ concepts for R-hat, ESS, divergences, LOO, WAIC, and posterior checks.
Includes utility scripts for diagnostic reporting, model comparison, and Bayesian model averaging.
Describes remedies for sampling problems such as divergences, low ESS, and high R-hat.
limitations: It does not fit models unless the user supplies data and executes the generated code.
It cannot validate domain assumptions without user-provided context and expert review.
Large models may require substantial compute resources outside the assistant session.
Some examples use pickle serialization, which should not load files from untrusted sources.

use_cases.title: Fit Research Models
use_cases.description: Design PyMC models with clear priors, likelihoods, diagnostics, and posterior checks for empirical research.

use_cases.title: Compare Predictive Models
use_cases.description: Use LOO, WAIC, and model averaging guidance to compare Bayesian alternatives with uncertainty.

use_cases.title: Debug Sampling Problems
use_cases.description: Interpret divergences, R-hat, ESS, and trace behavior, then choose practical reparameterization steps.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Model
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a dataset with [outcome] and predictors [predictors]. Recommend a PyMC model, priors, likelihood, and validation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a PyMC Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a PyMC workflow for [analysis goal]. Include data preparation, prior predictive checks, sampling settings, diagnostics, and posterior predictions.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Sampling Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these PyMC diagnostics: [diagnostic summary]. Explain the likely problems and propose changes to priors, parameterization, or sampling settings.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Bayesian Models
prompt_templates.prompt: I fit these PyMC models: [model summaries]. Plan a LOO or WAIC comparison, reliability checks, and model averaging strategy.

output_examples.input: Ask for a Bayesian regression plan for a continuous outcome with three predictors.
output_examples.output: The response recommends standardized predictors, weakly informative priors, a normal likelihood, prior checks, NUTS sampling, diagnostics, and posterior prediction.

output_examples.input: Ask why a hierarchical PyMC model has divergences and low effective sample size.
output_examples.output: The response explains likely funnel geometry, recommends non-centered parameterization, stronger scale priors, higher target acceptance, and follow-up diagnostics.

output_examples.input: Ask how to compare three fitted Bayesian models.
output_examples.output: The response outlines log likelihood storage, LOO comparison, Pareto-k reliability checks, interpretation of differences, and optional model averaging.

best_practices: Start with simple models, then add hierarchy, interactions, or time structure only when diagnostics support them.
Run prior and posterior predictive checks before interpreting parameter estimates.
Report uncertainty intervals, convergence diagnostics, and model comparison reliability together.
anti_patterns: Do not use flat priors when weakly informative priors express realistic domain bounds.
Do not interpret posterior summaries before checking R-hat, ESS, divergences, and trace behavior.
Do not load pickle files from untrusted sources when saving or sharing model artifacts.

faq.question: What type of work does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports PyMC model design, sampling, diagnostics, prediction, and model comparison for Bayesian analysis.

faq.question: Does it require PyMC experience?
faq.answer: No. It includes beginner workflows, but users should understand their data and modeling assumptions.

faq.question: Can it run MCMC sampling for me?
faq.answer: It can generate and explain code, but sampling runs in the user environment with installed dependencies.

faq.question: How does it handle model diagnostics?
faq.answer: It explains R-hat, effective sample size, divergences, trace plots, and posterior predictive checks.

faq.question: Can it compare multiple models?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers LOO, WAIC, Pareto-k reliability, interpretation of differences, and model averaging.

faq.question: What should users be careful about?
faq.answer: Users should review priors, validate assumptions, protect sensitive data, and avoid loading untrusted pickle files.
